messages.subject: findnextitem doesn't check criterion?
parts:
Hi Phil,

i use mirtCAT as a backend in a server and wrote a function that takes a response vector, updates the CAT with these responses and returns the next item. However, the function will always return an item and doesn't return NA when the criterion for the CAT is fulfilled. Am I missing an additional step besides  xx$des...@Update.thetas(xx$design, xx$person, xx$test) to update the criteria check?

Best, Felix


set.seed(1234)
nitems <- 50
itemnames <- paste0('Item.', 1:nitems)
a <- matrix(rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3))
d <- matrix(rnorm(nitems))
dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = 'dich')
mod <- mirt(dat, 1)
coef(mod, simplify=TRUE)

# simple math items
questions <- answers <- character(nitems)
choices <- matrix(NA, nitems, 5)
spacing <- floor(d - min(d)) + 1 #easier items have more variation in the options

for(i in 1:nitems){
  n1 <- sample(1:50, 1)
  n2 <- sample(51:100, 1)
  ans <- n1 + n2
  questions[i] <- paste0(n1, ' + ', n2, ' = ?')
  answers[i] <- as.character(ans)
  ch <- ans + sample(c(-5:-1, 1:5) * spacing[i,], 5)
  ch[sample(1:5, 1)] <- ans
  choices[i, ] <- as.character(ch)
}

df <- data.frame(Question=questions, Option=choices, 
                 Type = 'radio', stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


xx = mirtCAT(mo = mod, df = df, design_elements = TRUE, design = list(min_SEM =.8)) 

for (i in 1:30){
  xx <- updateDesign(xx, items = i, responses = 1)
  xx$des...@Update.thetas(xx$design, xx$person, xx$test)
}

findnextitem(xx)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: findnextitem doesn't check criterion?
parts:
Hi Felix,

The NA return option from findNextItem() is mainly useful when front-end users are supplying their own customNextItem definition. By default, it just finds the next item regardless of the stopping criteria (excluding running out of the item bank entirely). If it helps, see the local run function for mirtCAT which is used to evaluate CAT designs without the GUI:

https://github.com/philchalmers/mirtCAT/blob/master/R/run_pattern.R 

Perhaps what you are looking for is the internal Update.stop_now() function, which I'd be happy to wrap inside one of the objects to make available (like putting this in Des...@Update.stop_now()). HTH. 

Phil
